# Z1: Anthropic agent platform capabilities vs. a 10-plugin / ~44-agent architecture

Researched 2026-10-17. Tags: [P] primary page read in full or in the relevant part; [S] search summary only; [U] unverified.
Caveat: WebFetch summarises pages through a small model, so exact numbers are [P] to the page as summarised; hooks (273k chars) and subagents (111k chars) pages were read only for the first ~100k chars.

Target architecture assumed: 10 plugins; ~44 role-specific agents each embedding a byte-identical ~290-line constitution; schema-first JSON handoffs; default-fail binding gates with retry caps; orchestration by skills that spawn subagents.

## 1. Capabilities table

| Capability | What it is | Source + tag | Architectural implication |
|---|---|---|---|
| Subagent frontmatter | `name, description, model (sonnet/opus/haiku/fable/ID/inherit), tools, disallowedTools, permissionMode, maxTurns, background, effort (low..max), isolation: worktree, omitClaudeMd, memory (user/project/local), skills (preload, up to 32), hooks, mcpServers, autoCompactWindow, initialPrompt, experimental.cacheTtl (5m/1h)` | code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents [P] | Model/effort tiering per agent (haiku/low recon, opus/high gate) is native. `omitClaudeMd` and `skills:` preload make the constitution deliverable without copying it into 44 files. |
| Plugin-agent restrictions | Plugin-shipped subagents ignore `hooks`, `mcpServers`, `permissionMode` | sub-agents page [P] | A plugin agent cannot carry its own enforcement hooks. Gates must be enforced by plugin-level `hooks/hooks.json` (SubagentStop, PreToolUse), not agent frontmatter. |
| Spawn depth / concurrency | Default depth 3 below main; `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH`; 20 concurrent subagents (`..._MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS`); `Agent(x,y)` allowlist in tools | sub-agents page [P] | Skill -> orchestrator subagent -> worker is 2-3 deep: near the limit. Keep orchestration in the skill (depth 1). Use `tools: Agent(...)` to restrict who can spawn whom. |
| Subagent description budget | Error above 15,000 tokens of agent descriptions | sub-agents page [P] | 44 agents x long trigger-style descriptions across 10 plugins can hit this. Keep descriptions short, move detail to body. |
| Fork / background / resume | `/subtask` fork inherits full conversation; background subagents get a reduced tool set and cannot ask the user; `SendMessage` resumes a subagent with history; `maxTurns` makes results resumable | sub-agents page [P] | Retry loops can resume the same subagent with context instead of cold-spawning. Background workers cannot do `AskUserQuestion`: gate agents must never need a human mid-run. |
| Skills | SKILL.md + `description`, `when_to_use`, `disable-model-invocation`, `user-invocable`, `allowed-tools`, `context: fork` + `agent:` (skill runs in a subagent), `arguments`, `` !`cmd` `` dynamic injection, `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}`; bundled scripts; ~500-line guidance; after compaction only the most recent ~5K tokens per skill is kept | code.claude.com/docs/en/skills [P] | `context: fork` is a native "skill spawns one agent" with no extra layer. Dynamic injection lets a skill pre-compute deterministic facts (git state, validator output) before the model sees it. Skill content lost to compaction on long runs. |
| Progressive disclosure | Metadata at startup; SKILL.md on trigger; linked files on demand | anthropic.com/engineering/equipping-agents-for-the-real-world-with-agent-skills [P] | Constitution should be a loaded-on-demand reference, not 290 inlined lines x 44. |
| Plugin bundle | `skills, commands, agents, hooks, mcpServers, lspServers, outputStyles, workflows (.js), monitors, themes, bin/ (on PATH), settings.json (agent, subagentStatusLine), userConfig, dependencies, channels, experimental.evals`; `version` pins; `claude plugin validate [--strict]`; `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/DATA` | code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference [P] | A plugin can ship deterministic scripts (`bin/`), workflows, monitors and cross-plugin `dependencies`. Plugin root `CLAUDE.md` is NOT loaded (validate warns). Ten plugins sharing `shared/` need dependency declarations or duplication. |
| `claude plugin eval` | Runs a plugin's `evals/` cases in isolated non-interactive sessions; 3 runs/case default; graders: regex, tool_used, file, llm rubric (judge); with-plugin vs no-plugin baseline (Δ); report HTML; CI threshold; v2.1.269+; costs real tokens; `experimental.evals` dir | code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-evals [P] | Native, vendor-supported replacement/complement for a repo-specific `mason:evaluate`. The baseline arm answers "does the plugin help vs. bare Claude?", which a 44-agent set must justify. Reports only the final reply/transcript/file, so hand-off schema validity is gradable via file graders. |
| Hooks | ~36 events incl. PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SubagentStart/Stop, TaskCreated/TaskCompleted, TeammateIdle, PreCompact, PermissionDenied; handler types command, http, mcp_tool, prompt, agent (experimental); Stop/SubagentStop `decision:"block"` + reason forces continuation; exit code 2 blocks; PreToolUse can rewrite input | code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks [P, first 100k chars] | A real deterministic gate: a SubagentStop/Stop command hook that runs a JSON-schema validator and blocks until the output validates replaces prompt-level "you must emit valid verdict@3". The docs summary did not mention `stop_hook_active` or loop caps [U]; retry caps must be implemented in the hook (counter file keyed on `agent_id`). |
| Agent teams | Experimental, off by default (`CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1`); lead + peer sessions, shared task list, mailbox messaging; reuse subagent definitions (tools, model, body; `skills` and plugin hooks NOT applied); no nested teams; no resume | code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-teams [P] | Not a basis for a plugin pipeline: experimental, interactive-only, not in `-p`/SDK. Note: enabling it silently turns named subagents into teammates. |
| Dynamic workflows | JS script run by a runtime; `agent()`, `pipeline()`, `parallel()`, `phase()`; `schema` option returns validated JSON (5 retries); resumable; 16 concurrent default, 1,000 agents/run; plugins ship `workflows/*.js`; script holds loop state so lead context holds only the final answer | code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows [P] | The closest native equivalent to "skill spawns subagents with schema handoffs + retry caps", but deterministic and resumable. Intermediate artifacts stay in variables (no context bleed). No mid-run user input; no `import`. |
| Permission modes / auto mode | Auto mode: a second-model classifier approves actions; default starting mode in v2.1.283+ interactive; classifier also reviews inter-agent messages and treats relayed approvals as untrusted | permission-modes [P, partly]; agent-teams [P] | Plugins cannot set `permissionMode` on agents; gates must not rely on prompts for approval. Script-computed prompts are marked as non-user text for the classifier. |
| Worktree isolation | `isolation: worktree` on a subagent; `/batch` splits one change into 5-30 worktree subagents | sub-agents, agents pages [P] | Write-capable workers (smith:implementer) can be isolated natively; no need for bespoke branch handling. |
| Memory | `memory:` frontmatter -> `.claude/agent-memory/<name>/MEMORY.md` (first 200 lines/25KB injected) | sub-agents page [P] | Native cross-session learning per agent; only for agents that benefit, else it adds context. |
| Routines / scheduling / Monitor / plugin monitors | Cloud scheduled routines; plugin `monitors` run only in interactive sessions | agents + plugins-reference pages [P] | Drift checks (`scribe:spec-drift`) could run as scheduled routines, not on-demand only. |
| Managed Agents (API) | Hosted harness in managed sandbox; Agent/Environment/Session/Events; beta (`managed-agents-2026-04-01`); multiagent orchestration (subagents, dynamic workflows, advisor); scheduled deployments; not ZDR/HIPAA eligible | platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/overview, /multiagent-orchestration [P] | Off-CLI path for running the same agent definitions headless. |
| Models | Fable 5.1 (`claude-fable-5-1`, 2026-09-01, $10/$50, always-on adaptive thinking, default effort high); Opus 5.5 (2026-09-22, $4/$20, default effort medium); Sonnet 5.5 ($2/$10, effort high); Haiku 5.5 (from $0.10/$0.50). All: 1M context, 128K max output, Jun 2026 cutoff. Effort low/medium/high/xhigh/max | platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview, /fable-5-1/overview, /opus-5-5/overview [P] | 1M context removes the main reason to split work for window size. Extended-thinking `budget_tokens` no longer accepted; thinking cannot be disabled on Opus 5.5 / Fable 5.1; forced `tool_choice` returns 400. Effort is the cost lever, not agent count. |
| Reported autonomy | Opus 5.5: customer reports of 18+ h unattended runs, 680k-line migration < 1 day, 9.5 h C-to-Rust translation; Fable 5.1: 38 h unattended ML run (vendor/customer testimonials) | anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5; /claude-fable-and-mythos-5-1 [P, marketing testimonials, not controlled] | Long single-agent runs are now credible; retry-capped micro-stages sized for 2024-era 30-minute horizons are likely over-segmented. Treat as testimony, not benchmark. |
| Prompt caching | 5m default, 1h at 2x write; read = 0.05x on Opus/Sonnet 5.5, 0.025x on Fable 5.1; min cacheable 512 tokens; prefix order tools -> system -> messages; subagent/workflow requests default to 5m TTL (`subagentPromptCacheTtl: 1h`); only agents with the same model, effort, agent type, tools, schema and cwd share a prefix | prompt-caching [P]; workflows page [P]; fable-5-1 overview [P] | A byte-identical constitution only saves money if it is the first block AND the agents share model/effort/tools. 44 agents with distinct types/tools/models mostly will not share a cache prefix, so the "identical constitution" pays full input price per agent type. [inference] |
| Context editing / compaction / memory tool | Server-side tool-result and thinking-block clearing (beta `context-management-2025-06-27`); `compact-2026-09-04` on-demand compaction (beta); memory tool `memory_20250818`; Claude Code `autoCompactWindow` per subagent | context-editing page [P]; opus-5-5 whats-new [P] | Long single-agent sessions are mechanically supported; compaction can drop constraints (Fable guide: "tell the model what to preserve in compaction summaries") [P]. |
| Tool search / programmatic tool calling / structured outputs | `defer_loading` + regex/BM25 tool search (>85% definition-token reduction; accuracy degrades past 30-50 tools); strict tool use and structured outputs replace forced tool use on 5.x models | tool-search-tool [P]; opus-5-5 whats-new [P] | JSON handoffs can be API-enforced (strict/structured outputs) and workflow `agent({schema})` enforces them in Claude Code; hand-written schema repair loops are redundant there. |
| Vision / computer use / browser | `computer_toolset_20260801`, `browser_toolset_20260801`; Opus 5.5 reads dense charts without tools; Fable 5.1 does better with crop/zoom tools | opus-5-5 whats-new [P]; fable prompting guide [P] | Front-end verification (render, screenshot, inspect) is a first-class agent capability; a separate "visual QA" agent is no longer needed for perception alone. |

## 2. Features that make parts of the architecture redundant or risky

1. **290-line constitution copied into 44 agent files.** Redundant given `skills:` preload, shared reference files loaded via progressive disclosure, and `omitClaudeMd`; risky because cache sharing is per (model, effort, type, tools) [P], so byte-identity buys little; and the 15,000-token agent-description cap [P] plus constitution drift risk (a byte-identity validator becomes load-bearing). Anthropic's own guidance: "minimal set of information that fully outlines expected behavior" [P: effective-context-engineering]. Counterpoint: Fable 5.1 follows existing prompts "without changes" [P], so shrinking is a quality-eval question, not a forced move.
2. **Prompt-enforced "default-fail" gates.** A gate agent is a model asked to be skeptical. Anthropic's harness post found self/peer evaluators need heavy calibration and drift lenient [P: harness-design-long-running-apps]; the multi-agent blog names the "early victory problem" for verifiers [P]. A Stop/SubagentStop hook running a validator is deterministic and cannot be talked out of failing.
3. **Retry caps expressed in prose.** Hooks and workflows can count; the model cannot reliably. Workflows cap structured-output retries at 5 natively [P].
4. **Skills that spawn subagents turn by turn.** Docs state Claude is then the orchestrator and every result lands in its context window; workflows move loops and intermediate results into script variables [P]. Role-pipeline orchestration by a model carries the "orchestrator failure" modes (duplicate work, vague delegation) [P].
5. **Role-by-pipeline-stage agents.** Anthropic's multi-agent guide names splitting by problem type (planner/implementer/tester/reviewer) as the anti-pattern; prefers context-centric decomposition [P: claude.com/blog/building-multi-agent-systems-when-and-how-to-use-them]. 44 role agents is exposed to this critique; the genuinely justified splits are verifier/adversary (clean context, minimal transfer) and parallel fan-out.
6. **Depth limits and plugin-agent restrictions.** Depth 3 default; plugin agents lose hooks/mcpServers/permissionMode [P]. Nested agent-calls-agent designs break or silently lose controls.
7. **Staleness of encoded assumptions.** "Every component in a harness encodes an assumption about what the model can't do... worth stress testing"; V2 harness removed sprint decomposition when Opus 4.6 arrived, cutting 6 h/$200 to 3.8 h/$125; evaluator value became conditional on task difficulty [P]. The agents split for 2024-2025 reliability limits are the prime suspects after Opus 5.5/Fable 5.1.
8. **Model-behaviour changes that break prompts.** Forced tool use rejected; thinking blocks bound to model and conversation (editing earlier turns invalidates them, 400 on new accounts); default effort changed (Opus 5.5 medium) [P]. Any agent that pins an old model, sets budget_tokens, or relies on `tool_choice` will fail.
9. **Agent teams enablement side-effect** (named subagents become teammates) [P].

## 3. Platform features the architecture does not use

- `claude plugin eval` with no-plugin baseline (Δ) in CI [P]; per-case 3 runs, llm/regex/tool_used/file graders.
- Plugin-level hooks as deterministic gates (schema validation on SubagentStop; PreToolUse path fences; TaskCompleted blocking) [P].
- `context: fork` + `agent:` in SKILL.md; `!`cmd`` dynamic context injection for deterministic recon (replaces a haiku "recon" agent for pure enumeration: git status, file lists, manifest) [P].
- Dynamic workflows shipped in the plugin (`workflows/`) with `agent({schema})`, `pipeline`/`parallel`, resumability, 16-way concurrency [P].
- `bin/` executables on PATH (validators, schema checkers) and `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}` for retry counters [P].
- `maxTurns` + `SendMessage` resume for repair loops with context retained [P].
- `isolation: worktree` for implementers; `memory:` for agents that accumulate conventions [P].
- Per-agent `effort` and `autoCompactWindow`; `experimental.cacheTtl: 1h` / `subagentPromptCacheTtl` for multi-minute fan-outs [P].
- Plugin `dependencies` to share one constitution/schema plugin across the 10 plugins instead of copying [P].
- Routines for scheduled drift/audit runs [P: agents page].
- Task budgets, per-message effort, compaction-on-demand (API) [P: opus-5-5 whats-new].

## 4. Evidence on multi-agent vs single-agent

| Claim | Evidence | Tag |
|---|---|---|
| Multi-agent beat single-agent on breadth research | Opus 4 lead + Sonnet 4 subagents beat single-agent Opus 4 by 90.2% on Anthropic's internal research eval | anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system [P] |
| Cost | Agents ~4x chat tokens; multi-agent ~15x (research system); later guidance: 3-10x vs single agent for equivalent tasks | same [P]; claude.com blog [P] |
| Where it works | Heavy parallelization, information exceeding one context, many complex tools, high-value tasks | research-system [P] |
| Where it does not | "Domains that require all agents to share the same context or involve many dependencies between agents"; most coding tasks ("LLM agents are not yet great at coordinating and delegating in real time") | research-system [P] |
| Three justified reasons | Context protection (>~1,000 tokens of irrelevant output), parallelism ("thoroughness, not speed"), specialization (agents with 20+ tools err); otherwise coordination costs exceed benefit | claude.com blog [P] |
| Anti-pattern | Splitting by role/problem type creates agents that spend more tokens communicating than working; decompose by context | claude.com blog [P] |
| Verifier failure | Verifiers declare victory after 1-2 tests; require explicit full-suite instructions | claude.com blog [P] |
| Orchestrator failures observed | 50+ subagents for simple queries, endless searches, duplicate work from vague delegation, sequential rather than parallel | research-system [P] |
| Simplicity default | "Find the simplest solution possible, only increasing complexity when needed"; frameworks obscure prompts; agents carry "compounding errors" risk | building-effective-agents [P] |
| Self-evaluation | Models praise their own mediocre work; a separate tuned evaluator is more tractable; but evaluator is conditionally valuable as models improve (essential at capability boundary, overhead otherwise) | harness-design-long-running-apps [P] |
| Single vs specialist open question | Anthropic's own long-running-harness post says it is "unclear" whether one generalist beats testing/QA/cleanup agents | effective-harnesses-for-long-running-agents [P] |
| Cost of harness | Solo agent 20 min/$9 vs full 3-agent harness 6 h/$200 vs simplified harness 3.8 h/$125 (quality was higher in harness, per the post's framing) | harness-design [P] |
| Claude Code docs | Teams "use significantly more tokens"; "for sequential tasks, same-file edits, or work with many dependencies, a single session or subagents are more effective"; subagents for side tasks that would flood the main context | agent-teams, agents pages [P] |
| Model-level shift | Opus 5.5 testimonial: "delegates to subagents far more effectively" (customer quote, not controlled) | anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5 [P, anecdotal] |
| Fable 5.1 guidance | Do not make the lead block on subagents; let it continue while they run (lower time at similar quality/tokens/cost on coding tasks) | prompting-claude-fable-5-1 [P] |
| Context rot | Recall degrades as context grows; sub-agents with clean contexts returning 1-2K-token summaries is the supported pattern | effective-context-engineering [P] |
| Eval guidance | Grade outcomes not paths; start with ~20 queries; use pass@k / pass^k; clean environment per trial; human transcript review | demystifying-evals; research-system [P] |

No source found that tests 40+ role-specialised agents in a linear plugin pipeline against a single agent with the same instructions [U]. The architecture's benefit is therefore untested by vendor evidence; the vendor's own test method (`claude plugin eval` with-arm vs without-arm) is the way to measure it.

## Source URLs
- https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents, /skills, /plugins-reference, /plugin-evals, /hooks, /agent-teams, /workflows, /agents, /permission-modes
- https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system, /building-effective-agents, /effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents, /effective-harnesses-for-long-running-agents, /harness-design-long-running-apps, /equipping-agents-for-the-real-world-with-agent-skills, /demystifying-evals-for-ai-agents, /writing-tools-for-agents

1	# Architecture review against current agent capabilities
2	
3	Status: proposal. Nothing here changes a plugin, schema, constitution or ADR. It tests each architectural assumption in `ARCHITECTURE.md` against what the current agent platforms can do, and adds the work packages that follow (WP-601 to WP-616, appended to the catalog's 144).
4	
5	Inputs: `ARCHITECTURE.md`; `evidence/Z1-claude-platform.md` (Claude Code and Anthropic engineering guidance); `evidence/Z2-other-harnesses.md` (Codex, Antigravity, Cursor, Copilot, standards); repo measurements taken for this review (section 1). Claims tagged [P] were read on a primary page, [S] come from a search summary, [I] are inference. Z1 read only the first 100k characters of the hooks and subagents pages, and the fetch tool summarizes pages, so quotes are the fetcher's wording.
6	
7	## 0. Corrections to earlier statements
8	
9	1. **The constitution is not 290 lines per agent.** Every one of the 44 agents embeds the same 6-line `<constitution>` block (one distinct block, checked by hash). The 290-line `shared/constitution.md` is the authoring-time rulebook; among agents only the `mason` auditor reads it at runtime. The research notes and `traceability/MAP-5-M-X.md` assumed a 290-line copy per agent, and so did my earlier summaries. The per-agent cost is about 6 lines. This lowers the priority of the "shrink the constitution" ablation (WP-62, ADR N10). See section 2, row 3.
10	2. **Cross-harness shape (from the user).** Codex has its own native plugin format, set up in this repo under `harnesses/codex/`; AGY's format is similar to Claude Code's and shares the authored tree. The cost is therefore one authored tree for Claude and AGY plus one native Codex tree, not three. The AGY risks are specific (section 6), not a third tree.

105	
106	- **New ADR N11, deterministic enforcement layer.** Gates and retry caps are enforced by hooks or workflows where the harness provides them; prose is the fallback. Touches the constitution's retry rules; sits beside N4 and N5.
107	- **N8 widens** to cover the manifest convergence (WP-610) and Codex hook parity.
108	- **N10 narrows** to backstory and skeleton ablations; the constitution-block question (WP-604) no longer needs an ADR unless the measurement says so.
109	- **ADR 003 may need a note** if WP-605 finds role-flavor splits worth merging; no change before that evidence.
110	- ADR 005 (artifact-agnostic gate) is unaffected: hooks and render evidence arrive as generic evidence kinds.
111

113	
114	- Multi-agent token cost is 3 to 15 times a single agent in Anthropic's own figures. WP-601 must price every new agent and workflow.
115	- The long-autonomy figures are testimonials, not benchmarks; the harness-simplification result is Opus 4.6-era and was not re-checked on 5.x.
116	- Hook loop behavior (`stop_hook_active`) was not confirmed; a blocking `Stop` hook without a counter can loop. WP-616 settles this before WP-602 ships.
117	- Codex hook counts, Antigravity 2.0 details and the 2026-10-19 workflow shutdown are search summaries; several vendor pages returned 403.
118	- The cache-sharing conclusion in row 3 is inference from the documented sharing conditions.
119	- No head-to-head comparison of Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity on UI tasks exists. VISTA and Vision2Web evaluate agents, not these harnesses against each other.
120	
121	## 10. Order of attack
122	
123	1. WP-609, WP-615, WP-616 (cheap, remove uncertainty), and WP-601 (the baseline everything else is measured against).
124	2. Wave 1 exploration modes, unchanged.
125	3. WP-602, WP-603, WP-605, WP-606, WP-613 in Wave 2 with the gate-hygiene work, so enforcement and the retry rules land together.
126	4. WP-607, WP-611, WP-614 with the Wave 3 visual-evidence bundle.
127	5. WP-608, WP-610, WP-612, WP-604 in Wave 4.

| Review bots and plan artifacts | Cursor Bugbot, Copilot review, Antigravity plan Artifacts | `ranger`, `sentinel`, `navigator` | Keep; ours add refutation and falsifiable gates |
| Code intelligence | LSP servers can be bundled in Claude plugins [P per Z1]; Netflix and JetBrains report 20 to 30% efficiency gains for Java | Language-service guidance in smith (commit `f10e6b8`) | Extend to UI facts (WP-611) |

## 4. Platform features this repo does not use yet

Plugin-level hooks as gates; `claude plugin eval` with a no-plugin baseline; plugin-shipped workflows; `bin/` validators; `SendMessage` resume for repair loops; `isolation: worktree`; per-agent `maxTurns` as a stall guard; `tools` allowlists; `skills` preload; subagent `memory` and a persistent plugin data directory for counters; plugin `dependencies`; routines for drift checks; bundled LSP servers.

## 5. Differentiators to protect

The harnesses natively do parallel agents, worktrees, browser capture, plan artifacts and review bots. None of them provides falsifiable specs, adversarial refutation, fail-by-default binding gates, or enforced self-audit [S per Z2]. These are why the plugins exist. The direction below moves the *enforcement* of those properties out of prose and into deterministic harness features, and leaves the properties themselves unchanged.

## 6. Direction: thinner prompts, thicker harness

1. **Move enforcement out of prose.** Retry caps, schema validity, "no pass without evidence refs" and self-audit become hook- or workflow-enforced where the harness allows, with the prompt-only path as the cross-harness fallback.
2. **Split agents by context, not by role.** Keep splits that buy independent or high-volume context (verifier, adversary, recon). Audit the rest against that criterion with a measured baseline.
3. **Design for longer autonomy.** Plans state outcomes, ownership and verification; progress is a resumable artifact; gates sit at boundaries, not inside every step.
4. **Make capabilities pluggable and detected.** Browser, worktree, memory and design-source access are adapters selected by capability, with identical artifacts out (`render-evidence`, `design-source`).
5. **Keep schemas as the cross-harness contract,** and share skill bodies where orchestration semantics are identical.
6. **Record the assumptions.** A register of what each component assumes the model cannot do, reviewed on each model generation (WP-609), so stale scaffolding is retired on evidence.

Cross-harness specifics:
- **Codex:** native plugin format under `harnesses/codex/`; custom agents are natively TOML [P], and this repo's policy keeps role cards as markdown resources (ADR N8 decides whether an optional generator may emit TOML). Subagents spawn only when asked or when a skill or AGENTS.md instructs it, so Codex orchestrator skills must say so. Re-check the generated tree against the new `extensions.com.openai` convention [P per Z2].
- **AGY:** plugin fields `plugin.json` (with `$schema`), optional `mcp_config.json`, `hooks.json`, `skills/`, `agents/`, `rules/`; workflows are not supported in plugins and stop working on 2026-10-19 [S], so author skills only. The public docs do not document the third-party marketplace schema, so the `$schema` reference in the root `marketplace.json` needs re-verifying [P per Z2]. Gemini CLI was retired in June [S].
- **Standards:** AGENTS.md, the Agent Skills `SKILL.md` standard, MCP 2026-07-28 (stateless core; Roots, Sampling and Logging deprecated), and Agent Plugins 1.0.0 as the portable manifest core.

Appended to the catalog's 144 (total 160). Waves follow `CATALOG.md` section 3.

## 8. ADR implications

- **New ADR N11, deterministic enforcement layer.** Gates and retry caps are enforced by hooks or workflows where the harness provides them; prose is the fallback. Touches the constitution's retry rules; sits beside N4 and N5.
- **N8 widens** to cover the manifest convergence (WP-610) and Codex hook parity.
- **N10 narrows** to backstory and skeleton ablations; the constitution-block question (WP-604) no longer needs an ADR unless the measurement says so.
- **ADR 003 may need a note** if WP-605 finds role-flavor splits worth merging; no change before that evidence.
- ADR 005 (artifact-agnostic gate) is unaffected: hooks and render evidence arrive as generic evidence kinds.

## 9. Risks and what is unverified

- Multi-agent token cost is 3 to 15 times a single agent in Anthropic's own figures. WP-601 must price every new agent and workflow.
- The long-autonomy figures are testimonials, not benchmarks; the harness-simplification result is Opus 4.6-era and was not re-checked on 5.x.
- Hook loop behavior (`stop_hook_active`) was not confirmed; a blocking `Stop` hook without a counter can loop. WP-616 settles this before WP-602 ships.
- Codex hook counts, Antigravity 2.0 details and the 2026-10-19 workflow shutdown are search summaries; several vendor pages returned 403.
- The cache-sharing conclusion in row 3 is inference from the documented sharing conditions.
- No head-to-head comparison of Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity on UI tasks exists. VISTA and Vision2Web evaluate agents, not these harnesses against each other.

## 10. Order of attack

1. WP-609, WP-615, WP-616 (cheap, remove uncertainty), and WP-601 (the baseline everything else is measured against).
2. Wave 1 exploration modes, unchanged.
3. WP-602, WP-603, WP-605, WP-606, WP-613 in Wave 2 with the gate-hygiene work, so enforcement and the retry rules land together.
4. WP-607, WP-611, WP-614 with the Wave 3 visual-evidence bundle.
5. WP-608, WP-610, WP-612, WP-604 in Wave 4.

#### TaskCompleted decision control

TaskCompleted hooks support two ways to control task completion:

* **Exit code 2**: the task is not marked as completed and the stderr message is fed back to the model as feedback.
* **JSON `{"continue": false, "stopReason": "..."}`**: when a teammate finishing its turn triggered the event, stops the teammate entirely, matching `Stop` hook behavior. The `stopReason` is shown to the user. When the `TaskUpdate` tool triggered the event, Claude Code ignores `continue: false`; exit code 2 still blocks the completion.

This example runs tests and blocks task completion if they fail:

```bash theme={null}
#!/bin/bash
INPUT=$(cat)
TASK_SUBJECT=$(echo "$INPUT" | jq -r '.task_subject')

# Run the test suite
if ! npm test 2>&1; then
  echo "Tests not passing. Fix failing tests before completing: $TASK_SUBJECT" >&2
  exit 2
fi

exit 0
```

### Stop

Runs when the main Claude Code agent has finished responding. Does not run if
the stoppage occurred due to a user interrupt. API errors fire
[StopFailure](#stopfailure) instead.

<Tip>
  The [`/goal`](/docs/en/goal) command is a built-in shortcut for a session-scoped prompt-based Stop hook. Use it when you want Claude to keep working toward a condition without writing hook configuration.
</Tip>

#### Stop input

In addition to the [common input fields](#common-input-fields), Stop hooks receive `stop_hook_active`, `last_assistant_message`, `background_tasks`, and `session_crons`. The `stop_hook_active` field is `true` when Claude Code is already continuing as a result of a stop hook. Check this value or process the transcript to avoid blocking on a condition that will never resolve.

Claude Code applies an 8-consecutive-continuation cap: after stop hooks have continued the turn eight times in a row, Claude Code overrides the next block and ends the turn. The count of consecutive continuations resets each time Claude calls a tool. To raise the cap, set [`CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP`](/docs/en/env-vars).

The `last_assistant_message` field contains the text content of Claude's final response, so hooks can access it without parsing the transcript file. For hooks that act on the just-completed turn, such as read-aloud or notification hooks, use this field rather than reading `transcript_path`: the transcript file isn't guaranteed to include the final message at Stop time on all versions.

The `background_tasks` and `session_crons` arrays let hooks distinguish "session is done" from "session is paused waiting for background work to wake it back up". Both arrays are present when the task registry is reachable and are empty when nothing is in flight or scheduled.

Each entry in `background_tasks` describes one in-flight task and uses these fields:

| Field | Description |
| :- | :- |
| `id` | Task identifier |
| `type` | Friendly task-type label such as `shell`, `subagent`, `monitor`, `workflow`, `teammate`, `cloud session`, or `MCP task`. Each label identifies which Claude Code feature created the task. Falls back to the raw discriminant for unrecognized types |
| `status` | Current task status |
| `description` | Free-text description, capped at 1000 characters with an in-string `… [+N chars]` marker when clipped |
| `command` | Shell command line, capped at 1000 characters. Present only for `shell` tasks |
| `agent_type` | Subagent type name. Present only for `subagent` tasks |
| `server` | MCP server name. Present only for `monitor` and `MCP task` tasks |
| `tool` | MCP tool name. Present only for `monitor` and `MCP task` tasks |
| `name` | Workflow name. Present only for `workflow` tasks |

Each entry in `session_crons` describes one session-scoped scheduled wakeup, sourced from `CronCreate`, `ScheduleWakeup`, and `/loop`:

| Field | Description |
| :- | :- |
| `id` | Cron task identifier |
| `schedule` | Cron expression, for example `0 9 * * 1-5` |
| `recurring` | `false` for one-shot wakeups whose schedule encodes a single fire time, `true` for tasks that re-fire on every match |
| `prompt` | Prompt submitted when the cron fires, capped at 1000 characters with the same `… [+N chars]` marker |

This example shows a Stop input with one in-flight shell task and one recurring cron:

```json theme={null}
{
  "session_id": "abc123",
  "transcript_path": "~/.claude/projects/.../00893aaf-19fa-41d2-8238-13269b9b3ca0.jsonl",
  "cwd": "/Users/...",
  "permission_mode": "default",
  "hook_event_name": "Stop",
  "stop_hook_active": true,
  "last_assistant_message": "I've completed the refactoring. Here's a summary...",
  "background_tasks": [
    {
      "id": "task-001",
      "type": "shell",
      "status": "running",
      "description": "tail logs",
      "command": "tail -f /var/log/syslog"
    }
  ],
  "session_crons": [
    {
      "id": "cron-001",
      "schedule": "0 9 * * 1-5",
      "recurring": true,
      "prompt": "check the build"
    }
  ]
}
```

#### Stop decision control

`Stop` and `SubagentStop` hooks can control whether Claude continues. In addition to the [JSON output fields](#json-output) available to all hooks, your hook script can return these event-specific fields:

| Field | Description |
| :- | :- |
| `decision` | `"block"` prevents Claude from stopping. Omit to allow Claude to stop |
| `reason` | Required when `decision` is `"block"`. Tells Claude why it should continue |
| `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` | Non-error feedback for Claude. The conversation continues so Claude can act on it, but unlike `decision: "block"` it is shown in the transcript as hook feedback rather than a hook error |

A hook that blocks by exiting 2 routes the same way as `reason`: Claude receives the stderr message as the explanation for why it should continue.

```json theme={null}
{
  "decision": "block",
  "reason": "Must be provided when Claude is blocked from stopping"
}
```

Use `additionalContext` when the hook is working as designed and giving Claude guidance, such as "run the test suite before finishing". It keeps the conversation going through the same loop protections as `decision: "block"`, namely the `stop_hook_active` input and the 8-consecutive-continuation cap, but the transcript labels it `Stop hook feedback` and no hook error notification is shown:

```json theme={null}
{
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "hookEventName": "Stop",
    "additionalContext": "Please run the test suite before finishing"
  }
}
```

### StopFailure

Runs instead of [Stop](#stop) when the turn ends due to an API error. Claude Code ignores the hook's output and exit code, apart from [`terminalSequence`](#emit-terminal-notifications). Use this to log failures, send alerts, or take recovery actions when Claude can't complete a response due to rate limits, authentication problems, or other API errors.

#### StopFailure input

In addition to the [common input fields](#common-input-fields), StopFailure hooks receive `error`, optional `error_details`, and optional `last_assistant_message`. The `error` field identifies the error type and is used for matcher filtering.

| Field | Description |
| :- | :- |
| `error` | Error type: `rate_limit`, `overloaded`, `authentication_failed`, `oauth_org_not_allowed`, `account_on_hold`, `billing_error`, `invalid_request`, `model_not_found`, `server_error`, `max_output_tokens`, `cloud_credential_error`, or `unknown` |
| `error_details` | Additional details about the error, when available |
| `last_assistant_message` | The rendered error text shown in the conversation. Unlike `Stop` and `SubagentStop`, where this field holds Claude's conversational output, for `StopFailure` it contains the API error string itself, such as `"API Error: Rate limit reached"` |

```json theme={null}
{
  "session_id": "abc123",
  "transcript_path": "/Users/.../.claude/projects/.../00893aaf-19fa-41d2-8238-13269b9b3ca0.jsonl",
  "cwd": "/Users/...",
  "hook_event_name": "StopFailure",
  "error": "rate_limit",
  "error_details": "429 Too Many Requests",
  "last_assistant_message": "API Error: Rate limit reached"
}
```

StopFailure hooks have no decision control. They run for notification and logging purposes only.

### TeammateIdle

Runs when an [agent team](/docs/en/agent-teams) teammate is about to go idle after finishing its turn. Use this to enforce quality gates before a teammate stops working, such as requiring passing lint checks or verifying that output files exist.

TeammateIdle hooks don't support matchers and fire on every occurrence.

Check this value or process the transcript to avoid blocking on a condition that will never resolve.

Claude Code applies an 8-consecutive-continuation cap: after stop hooks have continued the turn eight times in a row, Claude Code overrides the next block and ends the turn. The count of consecutive continuations resets each time Claude calls a tool. To raise the cap, set [`CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP`](/docs/en/env-vars).

The `last_assistant_message` field contains the text content of Claude's final response, so hooks can access it without parsing the transcript file. For hooks that act on the just-completed turn, such as read-aloud or notification hooks, use this field rather than reading `transcript_path`: the transcript file isn't guaranteed to include the final message at Stop time on all versions.

The `background_tasks` and `session_crons` arrays let hooks distinguish "session is done" from "session is paused waiting for background work to wake it back up". Both arrays are present when the task registry is reachable and are empty when nothing is in flight or scheduled.

Each entry in `background_tasks` describes one in-flight task and uses these fields:

| Field | Description |
| :- | :- |
| `id` | Task identifier |
| `type` | Friendly task-type label such as `shell`, `subagent`, `monitor`, `workflow`, `teammate`, `cloud session`, or `MCP task`. Each label identifies which Claude Code feature created the task. Falls back to the raw discriminant for unrecognized types |
| `status` | Current task status |
| `description` | Free-text description, capped at 1000 characters with an in-string `… [+N chars]` marker when clipped |
| `command` | Shell command line, capped at 1000 characters. Present only for `shell` tasks |
| `agent_type` | Subagent type name. Present only for `subagent` tasks |
| `server` | MCP server name. Present only for `monitor` and `MCP task` tasks |
| `tool` | MCP tool name. Present only for `monitor` and `MCP task` tasks |
| `name` | Workflow name. Present only for `workflow` tasks |

Each entry in `session_crons` describes one session-scoped scheduled wakeup, sourced from `CronCreate`, `ScheduleWakeup`, and `/loop`:

| Field | Description |
| :- | :- |
| `id` | Cron task identifier |
| `schedule` | Cron expression, for example `0 9 * * 1-5` |
| `recurring` | `false` for one-shot wakeups whose schedule encodes a single fire time, `true` for tasks that re-fire on every match |
| `prompt` | Prompt submitted when the cron fires, capped at 1000 characters with the same `… [+N chars]` marker |

This example shows a Stop input with one in-flight shell task and one recurring cron:

```json theme={null}
{
  "session_id": "abc123",
  "transcript_path": "~/.claude/projects/.../00893aaf-19fa-41d2-8238-13269b9b3ca0.jsonl",
  "cwd": "/Users/...",
  "permission_mode": "default",
  "hook_event_name": "Stop",
  "stop_hook_active": true,
  "last_assistant_message": "I've completed the refactoring. Here's a summary...",
  "background_tasks": [
    {
      "id": "task-001",
      "type": "shell",
      "status": "running",
      "description": "tail logs",
      "command": "tail -f /var/log/syslog"
    }
  ],
  "session_crons": [
    {
      "id": "cron-001",
      "schedule": "0 9 * * 1-5",
      "recurring": true,
      "prompt": "check the build"
    }
  ]
}
```

#### Stop decision control

`Stop` and `SubagentStop` hooks can control whether Claude continues. In addition to the [JSON output fields](#json-output) available to all hooks, your hook script can return these event-specific fields:

| Field | Description |
| :- | :- |
| `decision` | `"block"` prevents Claude from stopping. Omit to allow Claude to stop |
| `reason` | Required when `decision` is `"block"`. Tells Claude why it should continue |
| `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` | Non-error feedback for Claude. The conversation continues so Claude can act on it, but unlike `decision: "block"` it is shown in the transcript as hook feedback rather than a hook error |

A hook that blocks by exiting 2 routes the same way as `reason`: Claude receives the stderr message as the explanation for why it should continue.

```json theme={null}
{
  "decision": "block",
  "reason": "Must be provided when Claude is blocked from stopping"
}
```

Use `additionalContext` when the hook is working as designed and giving Claude guidance, such as "run the test suite before finishing". It keeps the conversation going through the same loop protections as `decision: "block"`, namely the `stop_hook_active` input and the 8-consecutive-continuation cap, but the transcript labels it `Stop hook feedback` and no hook error notification is shown:

```json theme={null}
{
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "hookEventName": "Stop",
    "additionalContext": "Please run the test suite before finishing"
  }
}
```

### StopFailure

Runs instead of [Stop](#stop) when the turn ends due to an API error. Claude Code ignores the hook's output and exit code, apart from [`terminalSequence`](#emit-terminal-notifications). Use this to log failures, send alerts, or take recovery actions when Claude can't complete a response due to rate limits, authentication problems, or other API errors.

#### StopFailure input

In addition to the [common input fields](#common-input-fields), StopFailure hooks receive `error`, optional `error_details`, and optional `last_assistant_message`. The `error` field identifies the error type and is used for matcher filtering.

| Field | Description |
| :- | :- |
| `error` | Error type: `rate_limit`, `overloaded`, `authentication_failed`, `oauth_org_not_allowed`, `account_on_hold`, `billing_error`, `invalid_request`, `model_not_found`, `server_error`, `max_output_tokens`, `cloud_credential_error`, or `unknown` |
| `error_details` | Additional details about the error, when available |
| `last_assistant_message` | The rendered error text shown in the conversation. Unlike `Stop` and `SubagentStop`, where this field holds Claude's conversational output, for `StopFailure` it contains the API error string itself, such as `"API Error: Rate limit reached"` |

```json theme={null}
{
  "session_id": "abc123",
  "transcript_path": "/Users/.../.claude/projects/.../00893aaf-19fa-41d2-8238-13269b9b3ca0.jsonl",
  "cwd": "/Users/...",
  "hook_event_name": "StopFailure",
  "error": "rate_limit",
  "error_details": "429 Too Many Requests",
  "last_assistant_message": "API Error: Rate limit reached"
}
```

StopFailure hooks have no decision control. They run for notification and logging purposes only.

### TeammateIdle

Runs when an [agent team](/docs/en/agent-teams) teammate is about to go idle after finishing its turn. Use this to enforce quality gates before a teammate stops working, such as requiring passing lint checks or verifying that output files exist.

TeammateIdle hooks don't support matchers and fire on every occurrence.

### SubagentStart

Runs when Claude spawns a subagent with the Agent tool, when Claude [resumes a subagent](/docs/en/sub-agents#resume-subagents), and each time an in-process [agent team](/docs/en/agent-teams) teammate handles a new message. Supports matchers to filter by agent type name. For built-in agents, this is the agent name like `general-purpose`, `Explore`, or `Plan`. For [custom subagents](/docs/en/sub-agents), this is the `name` field from the agent's frontmatter, not the filename.

For subagents shipped by a [plugin](/docs/en/plugins/overview), the agent type is the plugin-scoped identifier such as `my-plugin:reviewer`, not the bare frontmatter name. The colon places a plugin-scoped name on the regular-expression path, so anchor the matcher with `^` and `$` for an exact match: `^my-plugin:reviewer$`.

#### SubagentStart input

In addition to the [common input fields](#common-input-fields), SubagentStart hooks receive `agent_id` with the unique identifier for the subagent and `agent_type` with the agent name that the matcher filters on.

```json theme={null}
{
  "session_id": "abc123",
  "transcript_path": "/Users/.../.claude/projects/.../00893aaf-19fa-41d2-8238-13269b9b3ca0.jsonl",
  "cwd": "/Users/...",
  "hook_event_name": "SubagentStart",
  "agent_id": "agent-abc123",
  "agent_type": "Explore"
}
```

SubagentStart hooks can't block subagent creation, but they can inject context into the subagent. In addition to the [JSON output fields](#json-output) available to all hooks, you can return:

| Field | Description |
| :- | :- |
| `additionalContext` | String added to the subagent's context at the start of its conversation, before its first prompt. See [Add context for Claude](#add-context-for-claude) |

```json theme={null}
{
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "hookEventName": "SubagentStart",
    "additionalContext": "Follow security guidelines for this task"
  }
}
```

When the hook runs again for the same subagent, Claude Code injects the returned context only when the subagent's context doesn't already hold the copy from an earlier run. The copy injected at launch stays in place, leaving the subagent's [prompt cache](/docs/en/prompt-caching#subagents-and-the-cache) intact. After [auto-compaction](/docs/en/sub-agents#auto-compaction) discards that copy, Claude Code injects the next run's context again.

### SubagentStop

Runs when a Claude Code subagent has finished responding. Matches on agent type, same values as SubagentStart.

#### SubagentStop input

In addition to the [common input fields](#common-input-fields), SubagentStop hooks receive `stop_hook_active`, `agent_id`, `agent_type`, `agent_transcript_path`, and `last_assistant_message`. The `agent_type` field is the value used for matcher filtering. The `transcript_path` is the main session's transcript, while `agent_transcript_path` is the subagent's own transcript stored in a nested `subagents/` folder. The `last_assistant_message` field contains the text content of the subagent's final response, so hooks can access it without parsing the transcript file.

Not every SubagentStop event comes from a subagent Claude spawned. Claude Code also runs internal agents for some of its own features, such as [prompt suggestions](/docs/en/interactive-mode#prompt-suggestions) and [`/btw` side questions](/docs/en/interactive-mode#side-questions-with-%2Fbtw), and SubagentStop fires when one of those finishes too. For those events, `agent_type` is the agent name the session itself runs as, such as one set with [`--agent`](/docs/en/cli-reference#cli-flags) or the [`agent` setting](/docs/en/settings-reference#agent), and an empty string when the session runs without one.

A `matcher` that names agent types doesn't match an empty `agent_type`. A hook whose matcher is omitted, `""`, or `"*"`, or is a regular expression that matches an empty string, runs for events with an empty `agent_type` too.

On Claude Code v2.1.271 or later, a subagent that runs with the [`SubagentHandback`](/docs/en/tools-reference) tool delivers its report through that tool before it stops. The `last_assistant_message` field then holds the subagent's closing text, if any, which is not the delivered report. The report is that call's `message` input, which a `PreToolUse` or `PostToolUse` hook matched on `SubagentHandback` receives as `tool_input.message`.

SubagentStop hooks also receive the `background_tasks` and `session_crons` arrays described under [Stop input](#stop-input). Both arrays are scoped to the parent session, not the subagent.

```json theme={null}
{
  "session_id": "abc123",
  "transcript_path": "~/.claude/projects/.../abc123.jsonl",
  "cwd": "/Users/...",
  "permission_mode": "default",
  "hook_event_name": "SubagentStop",
  "stop_hook_active": false,
  "agent_id": "def456",
  "agent_type": "Explore",
  "agent_transcript_path": "~/.claude/projects/.../abc123/subagents/agent-def456.jsonl",
  "last_assistant_message": "Analysis complete. Found 3 potential issues...",
  "background_tasks": [],
  "session_crons": []
}
```

SubagentStop hooks use the same decision control format as [Stop hooks](#stop-decision-control), including `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` with `hookEventName` set to `"SubagentStop"`, for non-error feedback that keeps the subagent running. Returning `decision: "block"` with a `reason` keeps the subagent running and delivers `reason` to the subagent as its next instruction. A hook that blocks by exiting 2 delivers its stderr message the same way. To inject context into the parent session after a subagent returns, use a [`PostToolUse`](#posttooluse) hook on the `Agent` tool instead.

# Hooks reference > Reference for Claude Code hook events, configuration schema, JSON input/output formats, exit codes, async hooks, HTTP hooks, prompt hooks, and MCP tool hooks. For a quickstart guide with examples, see [Automate actions with hooks](/docs/en/hooks-guide). Hooks are user-defined shell commands, HTTP endpoints, MCP tool calls, LLM prompts, or subagents that execute automatically at specific points in Claude Code's lifecycle. Claude Code fires the same hook events wherever it runs: sessions in the terminal, IDE extensions, the [Desktop app](/docs/en/desktop-quickstart), and [cloud sessions](/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web). Use this reference to look up event schemas, configuration options, JSON input/output formats, and advanced features like async hooks, HTTP hooks, and MCP tool hooks. A plugin can also register hooks as JavaScript functions that Claude Code calls in its own process, which can draw in the interface as well as act on events. A plugin that does is a [mod](/docs/en/plugins/mods/overview), and those function hooks are covered in [React to events](/docs/en/plugins/mods/events) rather than here. The hooks on this page keep working alongside mods. ## Hook lifecycle Claude Code runs hooks at specific points during a session. When an event fires and a matcher matches, Claude Code passes JSON context about the event to your hook handler. For command hooks, input arrives on stdin. For HTTP hooks, it arrives as the POST request body. Your handler can then inspect the input, take action, and optionally return a decision. Events fall into three cadences: * per session: `SessionStart` and `SessionEnd` * per turn: `UserPromptSubmit`, `Stop`, and `StopFailure` * on every tool call inside the agentic loop: `PreToolUse` and `PostToolUse`, except [`EndConversation`](/docs/en/tools-reference#endconversation-tool-behavior) calls, which skip both
The table below summarizes when each event fires. The [Hook events](#hook-events) section documents the full input schema and decision control options for each one. | Event | When it fires | | :- | :- | | `SessionStart` | When a session begins or resumes | | `Setup` | When you start Claude Code with `--init-only`, or with `--init` or `--maintenance` in `-p` mode. For one-time preparation in CI or scripts | | `UserPromptSubmit` | When a prompt is submitted, before Claude processes it. Also fires on [turns Claude Code starts on its own](/docs/en/hooks#userpromptsubmit) | | `UserPromptExpansion` | When a user-typed command expands into a prompt, before it reaches Claude. Can block the expansion | | `PreToolUse` | Before a tool call executes. Can block it | | `PermissionRequest` | When a tool call needs a permission decision | | `PermissionDenied` | When auto mode denies a tool call, including denials without a classifier verdict. Use JSON `hookSpecificOutput.retry: true` to tell the model it may retry the denied tool call. Claude Code ignores `retry` when the classifier produced no verdict | | `PostToolUse` | After a tool call succeeds | | `PostToolUseFailure` | After a tool call fails | | `PostToolBatch` | After a full batch of parallel tool calls resolves, before the next model call | | `Notification` | When Claude Code sends a notification | | `MessageDisplay` | While assistant message text is displayed | | `SubagentStart` | When a subagent is spawned | | `SubagentStop` | When a subagent finishes | | `TaskCreated` | When a task is being created via `TaskCreate` | | `TaskCompleted` | When a task is being marked as completed | | `Stop` | When Claude finishes responding | | `StopFailure` | When the turn ends due to an API error | | `TeammateIdle` | When an [agent team](/docs/en/agent-teams) teammate is about to go idle | | `InstructionsLoaded` | When a CLAUDE.md or `.claude/rules/*.md` file is loaded into context. Fires at session start and when files are lazily loaded during a session | | `ConfigChange` | When a configuration file changes during a session | | `CwdChanged` | When the working directory changes, for example when Claude executes a `cd` command. Useful for reactive environment management with tools like direnv | | `DirectoryAdded` | When a working directory is added mid-session via `/add-dir` or the SDK `register_repo_root` control request | | `FileChanged` | When a watched file changes on disk. The `matcher` field specifies which filenames to watch | | `WorktreeCreate` | When a worktree is being created via `--worktree`, `isolation: "worktree"`, or for a background session. Replaces default git behavior | | `WorktreeRemove` | When a worktree that a `WorktreeCreate` hook created is being removed | | `PreCompact` | Before context compaction | | `PostCompact` | After context compaction completes | | `PreModelSwitch` | Before Claude Code applies a model switch that you or a client requested. Can block the switch | | `PostModelSwitch` | After the session's model changes, including changes Claude Code makes on its own, such as restoring the model when you resume a session | | `Elicitation` | When an MCP server requests user input during a tool call | | `ElicitationResult` | After a user responds to an MCP elicitation, before the response is sent back to the server | | `SessionEnd` | When a session terminates | ### How a hook resolves To see how the event, the matcher, and the handler fit together, consider this `PreToolUse` hook that blocks destructive shell commands. The `matcher` narrows to Bash tool calls and the `if` condition narrows further to Bash subcommands matching `rm *`, so `block-rm.sh` only spawns when both filters match: ```json theme={null} { "hooks": { "PreToolUse": [ { "matcher": "Bash", "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "if": "Bash(rm *)", "command": "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.claude/hooks/block-rm.sh", "args": [] } ] } ] } } ``` The script reads the JSON input from stdin, extracts the command, and returns a `permissionDecision` of `"deny"` if it contains `rm -rf`. Save it to `.claude/hooks/block-rm.sh` in your project and make it executable with `chmod +x .claude/hooks/block-rm.sh` so Claude Code can run it: ```bash theme={null} #!/bin/bash # .claude/hooks/block-rm.sh COMMAND=$(jq -r '.tool_input.command') if echo "$COMMAND" | grep -q 'rm -rf'; then jq -n '{ hookSpecificOutput: { hookEventName: "PreToolUse", permissionDecision: "deny", permissionDecisionReason: "Destructive command blocked by hook" } }' else exit 0 # no decision; normal permission flow applies fi ```

Define one or more [hook handlers](#hook-handler-fields) to run when matched See [How a hook resolves](#how-a-hook-resolves) above for a complete walkthrough with an annotated example. This page uses specific terms for each level: **hook event** for the lifecycle point, **matcher group** for the filter, and **hook handler** for the shell command, HTTP endpoint, MCP tool, prompt, or agent that runs. "Hook" on its own refers to the general feature. ### Hook locations Where you define a hook determines its scope: | Location | Scope | Shareable | | :- | :- | :- | | `~/.claude/settings.json` | All your projects | No, local to your machine | | `.claude/settings.json` | Single project | Yes, can be committed to the repo | | `.claude/settings.local.json` | Single project | No, gitignored when Claude Code saves a setting to it | | Managed policy settings | Organization-wide | Yes, admin-controlled | | [Plugin](/docs/en/plugins/overview) `hooks/hooks.json` | When plugin is enabled | Yes, bundled with the plugin | | [Skill](/docs/en/skills) frontmatter | The rest of the session once the skill is invoked. See [Hooks in skills and agents](#hooks-in-skills-and-agents) | Yes, defined in the skill file | | [Subagent](/docs/en/sub-agents) frontmatter | While that subagent is running | Yes, defined in the subagent file | [Cloud sessions](/docs/en/claude-code-on-the-web) don't read your local `~/.claude/settings.json`. In a [self-hosted environment](/docs/en/self-hosted-environments-configuration#permissions-and-tool-approval), Claude Code also runs the hooks the operator seeded from the runner host's `~/.claude/`, and it runs the hooks in the runner image's managed settings file when that file is among the [managed sources Claude Code applies](/docs/en/managed-settings#how-claude-code-combines-managed-sources), which by default means only when neither server-managed settings nor an MDM-delivered Claude Code policy supplies the managed tier. See [what carries over from your setup](/docs/en/cloud-environments#what-carries-over-from-your-setup) for which settings files and plugins, and so which hooks, reach a cloud session. For details on settings file resolution, see [settings](/docs/en/settings). Hooks from settings files, managed policy settings, and plugins also run inside [subagents](/docs/en/sub-agents). When a subagent calls a tool, tool events such as `PreToolUse` and `PostToolUse` fire the same configured hooks as in the main conversation, and the input carries the `agent_id` and `agent_type` [common input fields](#common-input-fields) that identify the subagent. Administrators can use [`allowManagedHooksOnly`](/docs/en/settings-reference#allowmanagedhooksonly) in [managed settings](/docs/en/managed-settings) to restrict which hooks run: * Your user, project, local, and plugin hooks are blocked. Hook entries merge across settings levels rather than replacing each other: user, project, and local settings add their own hooks without removing managed ones, and the [`disableAllHooks`](#disable-or-remove-hooks) setting can't disable managed hooks from outside managed settings. The [HTTP hook allowlists](/docs/en/settings-reference#hook-and-skill-settings) apply to hooks from every source, including managed policy settings: * `allowedHttpHookUrls`: when defined at any settings level, Claude Code runs an HTTP hook handler only if its URL matches the merged allowlist * `httpHookAllowedEnvVars`: when defined, Claude Code interpolates only the environment variables on that list into hook headers ### Matcher patterns The `matcher` field filters when hooks fire. How a matcher is evaluated depends on the characters it contains: | Matcher value | Evaluated as | Example | | :- | :- | :- | | `"*"`, `""`, or omitted | Match all | fires on every occurrence of the event | | Only letters, digits, `_`, `-`, spaces, `,`, and `\|` | Exact string, or list of exact strings separated by `\|` or `,` with optional surrounding whitespace | `Bash` matches only the Bash tool; `Edit\|Write` and `Edit, Write` each match either tool exactly; `code-reviewer` matches only that agent type | | Contains any other character | JavaScript regular expression, unanchored | `^Notebook` matches any tool whose name starts with `Notebook`; `mcp__memory__.*` matches every tool from the `memory` server | A matcher on the regular-expression path is tested with JavaScript's `RegExp.prototype.test`, which succeeds on a match anywhere in the value. `Edit.*` matches both `Edit` and `NotebookEdit`; wrap the pattern in `^` and `$`, as in `^Edit$`, when you need a whole-string match. `FileChanged` and `StopFailure` use a narrower exact-match set of letters, digits, `_`, and `|` only. A hyphen, space, or comma in a matcher for those two events keeps it on the regular-expression path, and only `|` separates alternatives. Every other event with matcher support in the table that follows accepts `|` or `,`. ### Hook handler fields Each object in the inner `hooks` array is a hook handler: the shell command, HTTP endpoint, MCP tool, LLM prompt, or agent that runs when the matcher matches. There are five types: * **[Command hooks](#command-hook-fields)** (`type: "command"`): run a shell command. Your script receives the event's [JSON input](#hook-input-and-output) on stdin and communicates results back through exit codes and stdout. * **[HTTP hooks](#http-hook-fields)** (`type: "http"`): send the event's JSON input as an HTTP POST request to a URL. The endpoint communicates results back through the response body using the same [JSON output format](#json-output) as command hooks. * **[MCP tool hooks](#mcp-tool-hook-fields)** (`type: "mcp_tool"`): call a tool on a configured [MCP server](/docs/en/mcp). The tool's text output is treated like command-hook stdout. * **[Prompt hooks](#prompt-and-agent-hook-fields)** (`type: "prompt"`): send a prompt to a Claude model for single-turn evaluation. The model returns its decision as JSON. See [Prompt-based hooks](#prompt-based-hooks). * **[Agent hooks](#prompt-and-agent-hook-fields)** (`type: "agent"`): spawn a subagent that can use tools like Read, Grep, and Glob to verify conditions before returning a decision. If you define the same handler in more than one settings file, it runs once. A plugin's or skill's copy of the same handler stays separate. If the current directory no longer exists, for example a worktree or temp directory that another shell deleted mid-session, Claude Code runs command hooks from the first of these that still exists: the directory the session started in, the project root, your home directory, or the system temp directory. Claude Code records a warning naming the fallback directory in the [debug log](#debug-hooks). For a worktree session that you start from the desktop app, see [What worktrees share with the main checkout](/docs/en/worktrees#what-worktrees-share-with-the-main-checkout). The `$CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE` environment variable is `"true"` in remote web environments and not set in the local CLI. Claude Code v2.1.199 and later sets [`$CLAUDE_CODE_BRIDGE_SESSION_ID`](/docs/en/env-vars) to the [Remote Control](/docs/en/remote-control) session ID while the local session has an active Remote Control connection. #### Common fields These fields apply to all hook types: | Field | Required | Description | | :- | :- | :- | | `type` | yes | `"command"`, `"http"`, `"mcp_tool"`, `"prompt"`, or `"agent"` | | `if` | no | [Permission rule syntax](/docs/en/permissions#permission-rule-syntax) to filter when this hook runs, such as `"Bash(git *)"` or `"Edit(*.ts)"`. The hook command only runs if the tool call matches the pattern. See the [Bash matching table](#bash-if-matching) for how Bash patterns evaluate against subcommands, `$()`, and backticks. Only evaluated on tool events: `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `PostToolUseFailure`, `PermissionRequest`, and `PermissionDenied`. On other events, a hook with `if` set never runs | | `timeout` | no | Seconds before canceling. Claude Code doesn't enforce it on a command hook you run with [`async: true`](#run-hooks-in-the-background). Defaults: 600 for `command`, `http`, and `mcp_tool`; 30 for `prompt`; 60 for `agent`. Claude Code lowers the `command`, `http`, and `mcp_tool` default to 30 on [`UserPromptSubmit`](#userpromptsubmit), [`PreModelSwitch`](#premodelswitch), and [`PostModelSwitch`](#postmodelswitch), and to 10 on [`MessageDisplay`](#messagedisplay). [`SessionEnd`](#sessionend) hooks share a 1.5-second budget; if your settings set a longer per-hook `timeout`, Claude Code raises the budget to match, up to 60 seconds | | `statusMessage` | no | Custom spinner message displayed while the hook runs | | `once` | no | If `true`, Claude Code removes the hook after its first successful run. A run that fails, blocks with exit code 2, or times out leaves the hook in place, so it runs again on the next matching event. Only honored for hooks declared in [skill frontmatter](#hooks-in-skills-and-agents); ignored in settings files and agent frontmatter | The `if` field holds exactly one permission rule. There is no `&&`, `||`, or list syntax for combining rules; to apply multiple conditions, define a separate hook handler for each. In an `if` condition for a file tool, a single-segment directory pattern like `"Edit(src/**)"` matches only the `src` directory in the working directory and the files under it. To match a directory named `src` at any depth, write `"Edit(**/src/**)"`. Before v2.1.214, `"Edit(src/**)"` matched a directory named `src` at any depth under the working directory.

How `if` patterns match Bash commands

For Bash patterns in the [`if` field](#common-fields), whether your hook command runs depends on the shape of the pattern and the Bash command Claude is invoking. Leading `VAR=value` assignments are stripped before matching. | `if` pattern | Bash command | Hook runs? | Why | | :- | :- | :- | :- | | `Bash(git *)` | `FOO=bar git push` | yes | leading assignments are stripped; `git push` matches | | `Bash(git *)` | `npm test && git push` | yes | each subcommand is checked; `git push` matches | | `Bash(rm *)` | `echo $(rm -rf /)` | yes | commands inside `$()` and backticks are checked; `rm -rf /` matches | | `Bash(rm *)` | `echo $(date)` | no | no subcommand matches `rm *` | | `Bash(git push *)` | `echo $(date)` | yes | patterns that specify more than the command name run the hook anyway on `$()`, backticks, or `$VAR` | When Claude Code can't determine which commands the Bash input runs, it runs your hook regardless of the pattern. Because the `if` filter is best-effort, use the [permission system](/docs/en/permissions) rather than a hook to enforce a hard allow or deny. #### Command hook fields In addition to the [common fields](#common-fields), command hooks accept these fields: | Field | Required | Description | | :- | :- | :- | | `command` | yes | Shell command to execute. With `args`, the executable to spawn directly. See [Exec form and shell form](#exec-form-and-shell-form) | | `args` | no | Argument list. When present, `command` is resolved as an executable and spawned directly with `args` as the argument vector, with no shell involved. See [Exec form and shell form](#exec-form-and-shell-form) | | `async` | no | If `true`, runs in the background without blocking. See [Run hooks in the background](#run-hooks-in-the-background) | | `asyncRewake` | no | If `true`, runs in the background and wakes Claude on exit code 2. The hook's stderr, or stdout if stderr is empty, is shown to Claude as a [system reminder](/docs/en/glossary#system-reminder) so it can react to a long-running background failure | | `shell` | no | Shell to use for this hook. Accepts `"bash"` or `"powershell"`. Defaults to `"bash"`, or to `"powershell"` on Windows when Git Bash isn't installed. Setting `"powershell"` runs the command via PowerShell on Windows. Does not require `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_POWERSHELL_TOOL` since hooks spawn PowerShell directly. Ignored when `args` is set | | `onFailure` | no | Whether the action that triggered the hook goes ahead when the hook fails: `"continue"` or `"block"`. See [Block the action when a hook fails](#block-the-action-when-a-hook-fails) for `"block"` and for leaving the field unset. Requires Claude Code v2.1.295 or later | ##### Exec form and shell form A command hook runs as exec form when `args` is set, and shell form when `args` is omitted. Set `args` whenever the hook references a [path placeholder](#reference-scripts-by-path), since each element is passed as one argument with no quoting. Omit `args` when you need shell features like pipes or `&&`, or when neither concern applies. **Exec form** runs when `args` is present. Claude Code resolves `command` as an executable on `PATH` and spawns it directly with `args` as the argument vector. There is no shell, so each `args` element is one argument exactly as written, and path placeholders like `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` are substituted into `command` and into each `args` element as plain strings. Special characters such as apostrophes, `$`, and backticks pass through verbatim because there is no shell to interpret them. No shell tokenization happens on any platform. **Shell form** runs when `args` is absent. The `command` string is passed to a shell: `sh -c` on macOS and Linux, Git Bash on Windows, or PowerShell when Git Bash isn't installed. Set the `shell` field to choose explicitly. The shell tokenizes the string, expands variables, and interprets pipes, `&&`, redirects, and globs. On Windows, exec form requires `command` to resolve to a real executable such as a `.exe`. The `.cmd` and `.bat` shims that npm, npx, eslint, and other tools install in `node_modules/.bin` are not executables and can't be spawned without a shell. To run them in exec form, invoke the underlying script with `node` directly, for example `"command": "node", "args": ["${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/node_modules/eslint/bin/eslint.js"]`. The `node` plus script-path pattern works on every platform because `node.exe` is a real binary. To run a `.cmd` or `.bat` shim by name, use shell form. This example runs a Node script bundled with a plugin. Exec form passes the resolved script path as one argument with no quoting: ```json theme={null} { "type": "command", "command": "node", "args": ["${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/format.js", "--fix"] } ``` The equivalent shell form needs quoting to handle paths with spaces or special characters: ```json theme={null} { "type": "command", "command": "node \"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}\"/scripts/format.js --fix" } ``` Both forms support the same [path placeholders](#reference-scripts-by-path), and both export them as the environment variables `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`, `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`, and `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA` on the spawned process, so a script can read `process.env.CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` regardless of how it was launched. To use an option value from a shell-form hook, read the `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_` environment variable, such as `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_WEBHOOK_URL` for a `webhook_url` option, or set `args` to switch the hook to exec form. Before v2.1.207, shell-form plugin hook commands also substituted `${user_config.*}`. In exec form, `command` is the executable name or path only. If `command` is a bare name with no path separator and contains whitespace alongside `args`, Claude Code logs a warning because the spawn will fail: there is no executable named `node script.js`. Move the extra tokens into `args`. Absolute paths with spaces, such as `C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe`, are a single valid executable and don't trigger the warning. #### HTTP hook fields In addition to the [common fields](#common-fields), HTTP hooks accept these fields: | Field | Required | Description | | :- | :- | :- | | `url` | yes | URL to send the POST request to | | `headers` | no | Additional HTTP headers as key-value pairs. Values support environment variable interpolation using `$VAR_NAME` or `${VAR_NAME}` syntax. Only variables listed in `allowedEnvVars` are resolved | | `allowedEnvVars` | no | List of environment variable names that may be interpolated into header values. References to unlisted variables are replaced with empty strings. Required for any env var interpolation to work | | `onFailure` | no | What happens to the action when the hook fails: `"continue"`, the default, or `"block"`. See [Block the action when a hook fails](#block-the-action-when-a-hook-fails). Requires Claude Code v2.1.295 or later | Claude Code sends the hook's [JSON input](#hook-input-and-output) as the POST request body with `Content-Type: application/json`. The response body uses the same [JSON output format](#json-output) as command hooks. Error handling differs from command hooks; see [HTTP response handling](#http-response-handling).
